Repeating the same topics completed last year
Selecting only topics that interest them personally
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: A personal development plan should be built from reflection on the role, feedback received and identified gaps.

n.0: Cost is a practical consideration, not a way of identifying need.
n.1: Development needs are individual, even in identical roles.
n.3: Repetition without a gap identified adds little.
n.4: Interest matters, but a plan should also address weaknesses.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse completes CPD on medical emergencies. Why is this topic recommended in every cycle?
o: Because it carries double CPD hours
Because it is a GDC recommended topic linked to patient safety
Because it is required by the practice insurer only
Because it is the only verifiable topic available
Because it replaces the need for other CPD
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Medical emergencies is a GDC recommended CPD topic because of its direct link to patient safety.

n.0: All verifiable CPD is counted at its actual duration.
n.2: Insurers may require it, but the GDC recommends it for patient safety.
n.3: A very wide range of verifiable topics exists.
n.4: It contributes to the total; it does not replace it.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked what reflection adds to a CPD activity. Which statement is most accurate?
o: Reflection converts non-verifiable CPD into verifiable CPD
Reflection helps identify how learning will change practice
Reflection is only required for clinical topics
Reflection is optional and adds nothing to the record
Reflection replaces the need for provider evidence
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Reflection connects the activity to practice, identifying what will be done differently as a result.

n.0: Verifiability depends on provider evidence, not reflection.
n.2: Reflection is valuable across all development outcomes.
n.3: Reflection is what links learning to changes in practice.
n.4: Evidence is still required for verifiable hours.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to carry out a task they have not been trained for. Which GDC principle is most directly engaged?
o: Have a clear and effective complaints procedure
Work within your professional knowledge and skills
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: GDC Standards require registrants to work within their knowledge, skills and professional competence.

n.0: Relevant when a patient complains, not when scope is exceeded.
n.1: Concerns confidentiality rather than competence.
n.2: Consent is separate from whether the clinician is trained to do the task.
n.3: An overarching principle, but the specific one here is working within your knowledge and skills.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse believes a colleague's practice is putting patients at risk. What does the GDC require them to do?
o: Discuss it only if asked directly by a manager
Raise the concern, even if they are not certain
Record it privately in case it is needed later
Report it only once they have gathered firm proof
Wait until harm has actually occurred
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The GDC requires registrants to raise concerns if patients are at risk, without waiting for certainty or proof.

n.0: The duty to raise concerns does not depend on being asked.
n.2: A private note does not protect the patients at risk.
n.3: Registrants should raise concerns without waiting for proof.
n.4: The duty exists precisely to prevent harm occurring.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse has taken additional training in oral health education. What determines whether they may now carry out this role?
o: Any additional course completed in the last five years
The nurse's own confidence in the subject
The practice owner's written permission alone
Their scope of practice and appropriate training
Whether another nurse in the practice already does it
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Additional skills may be undertaken only where they fall within scope of practice and appropriate training has been completed.

n.0: The course must be appropriate to the specific role, not merely recent.
n.1: Confidence is not a substitute for recognised training.
n.2: An employer cannot extend a registrant's scope of practice.
n.4: What a colleague does has no bearing on your own scope.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A patient asks a dental nurse to explain what treatment they need. What is the most appropriate response?
o: Describe the likely treatment based on the notes
Explain that this must be discussed with the dentist
Give a general opinion but avoid specifics
Offer the nurse's own view of what is needed
Tell the patient to look it up before their next visit
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Diagnosis and treatment planning fall outside the dental nurse's scope; the patient should be directed to the dentist.

n.0: Interpreting the plan for the patient is a diagnostic act.
n.2: A general opinion is still an opinion the nurse is not able to give.
n.3: Treatment need is diagnosed by the dentist.
n.4: Leaves the patient without an answer and without support.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is completing their annual GDC declaration. What must they confirm?
o: That the practice has completed its own CPD returns
That their employer is satisfied with their performance
That they have completed the required CPD and hold indemnity
That they have not received any complaints that year
That they intend to remain in dental nursing
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Registrants confirm at renewal that they have met CPD requirements and hold appropriate indemnity.

n.0: Declaration is personal to the registrant, not the practice.
n.1: Employer satisfaction is not a GDC registration requirement.
n.3: Complaints are handled separately and are not declared this way.
n.4: Intention is not part of the annual declaration.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse without indemnity arrangements continues to work chairside. Why is this a problem?
o: Indemnity is a legal and GDC requirement for registration
Indemnity is only needed for nurses taking radiographs
Indemnity is only required once a complaint is made
It affects the practice's insurance but not the nurse
It prevents the nurse from claiming CPD hours
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Appropriate indemnity or insurance is a condition of GDC registration and a legal requirement.

n.1: It applies to all registrants regardless of duties.
n.2: Cover must be in place before any concern arises.
n.3: The registrant carries a personal obligation.
n.4: CPD and indemnity are unrelated requirements.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse makes a mistake that could affect a patient's care. What does the duty of candour require?
o: Correct the record quietly and move on
Discuss it only if the patient notices
Report it to the GDC before telling anyone else
Tell the patient what happened and apologise
Wait until the outcome is known before saying anything
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The duty of candour requires being open with patients when something goes wrong, including an apology.

n.0: Amending records without telling the patient is the opposite of candour.
n.1: Candour is not conditional on being found out.
n.2: The patient should be told; not every incident requires GDC referral.
n.4: Patients should be told promptly, even while the outcome is uncertain.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is invited to an appraisal by their line manager. What is the main purpose of appraisal?
o: To decide whether the nurse's registration continues
To identify development needs and agree objectives
To record any complaints made during the year
To satisfy the practice's insurance requirements
To set the nurse's pay for the coming year
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Appraisal identifies development needs and agrees objectives, feeding directly into the personal development plan.

n.0: Registration is a matter for the GDC, not the employer.
n.2: Complaints are handled through a separate procedure.
n.3: Insurers do not drive the appraisal process.
n.4: Pay may be discussed, but development is the purpose.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A newly qualified dental nurse joins the practice. Which arrangement best supports their early development?
o: A structured induction with an identified mentor
Allowing them to work independently from the first day
Giving them the same objectives as an experienced nurse
Reviewing their progress at the end of the first year
Waiting until they raise any difficulties themselves
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: A structured induction with a named mentor gives new registrants support and a route to raise difficulties early.

n.1: Independence without support risks patient safety and confidence.
n.2: Objectives should reflect their stage of development.
n.3: Far too late to correct early difficulties.
n.4: New staff are often least likely to ask for help.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse records their CPD in a spreadsheet with dates, hours, outcomes and evidence. Why does mapping to development outcomes matter?
o: It allows hours to be doubled where two outcomes apply
It converts non-verifiable activity into verifiable activity
It is required only for registrants in their first cycle
It removes the need to retain certificates
It shows the CPD supports the GDC Standards
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The development outcomes link CPD activity to the Standards for the Dental Team, showing the learning supports practice.

n.0: Hours reflect actual duration regardless of how many outcomes apply.
n.1: Mapping does not change verifiability.
n.2: Mapping applies throughout a registrant's career.
n.3: Evidence must still be kept.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dentist asks a dental nurse to take a task on during a busy list. What makes delegation appropriate?
o: The nurse has been trained and is competent for the task
The nurse has seen the task performed several times
The nurse is willing to attempt it
The practice is short-staffed that day
The task is quick and unlikely to cause harm
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: A task may only be delegated to someone trained and competent to carry it out, and working within their scope.

n.1: Observation is not training and does not establish competence.
n.2: Willingness does not make a task within scope.
n.3: Pressure on staffing never justifies delegating beyond competence.
n.4: Risk is judged by the task, not by how long it takes.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A task has been delegated to a dental nurse by the dentist. Who retains overall responsibility for the patient's care?
o: Both equally, regardless of the task
The dental nurse who carried out the task
The dentist who delegated the task
Whoever recorded the entry in the notes
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The person delegating retains overall responsibility for the patient's care, while the person carrying out the task remains accountable for their own actions.

n.0: The nurse is accountable for their own actions, but overall responsibility stays with the delegating clinician.
n.1: The nurse is accountable for how they perform it, not for the decision to delegate.
n.3: Has no clinical responsibility for the patient.
n.4: Recording does not confer clinical responsibility.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is handing over to a colleague partway through a list. What information is most important to pass on?
o: How long each remaining appointment is booked for
The names of the patients still to be seen
The patient's treatment stage, any concerns and what remains to be done
Which instruments have already been used
Who is due to take the next break
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Handover should cover the clinical position: where treatment has reached, outstanding tasks and any concerns.

n.0: Useful scheduling detail, but it is not clinical handover.
n.1: Necessary but insufficient on its own.
n.3: Managed through decontamination rather than handover.
n.4: A staffing matter, not patient safety.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse disagrees with a colleague about how the surgery should be set up. What is the most professional approach?
o: Ask another colleague to decide between them
Discuss it calmly and agree an approach that follows practice policy
Do it their own way and say nothing
Raise it with the patient present to settle it quickly
Report the colleague to the practice manager immediately
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Professional disagreement should be resolved calmly and away from patients, with practice policy as the reference point.

n.0: Delegates a disagreement that the two of them can resolve.
n.2: Leaves an inconsistency that may affect patient safety.
n.3: Disagreement in front of a patient undermines confidence.
n.4: Escalation before any attempt to resolve it directly.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse notices the surgery is regularly running behind and turnaround is rushed. What is the most constructive action?
o: Accept it as normal for a busy practice
Raise it at a team meeting with suggestions for improvement
Reduce the decontamination steps to save time
Speak to patients about the delays as they arrive
Work through breaks to catch up
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Systemic problems are best raised through the team so the cause can be addressed rather than absorbed by individuals.

n.0: Rushed turnaround is a patient safety risk, not a fact of life.
n.2: Never acceptable; decontamination is not a variable.
n.3: Manages the symptom without addressing the cause.
n.4: Unsustainable and increases the risk of error through fatigue.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to supervise a trainee during a procedure. What does effective supervision require?
o: Allowing the trainee to work unobserved to build confidence
Being present and able to intervene, with clear limits agreed beforehand
Checking the trainee's work only at the end of the session
Leaving the trainee with written instructions
Remaining in the building but not the surgery
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Supervision means being available to intervene, with the trainee's limits agreed in advance.

n.0: Confidence is built safely under observation, not without it.
n.2: Too late to prevent an error during the procedure.
n.3: Instructions are no substitute for a supervisor who can intervene.
n.4: Being nearby is not the same as being able to intervene.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: Two nurses in a practice follow different decontamination routines. What is the main risk?
o: Instruments may be processed inconsistently and unsafely
Neither nurse will be able to claim CPD hours
One nurse will work faster than the other
Stock will be used at different rates
The practice will need to buy more equipment
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Decontamination must follow a single agreed protocol; variation between staff makes outcomes unreliable.

n.1: CPD is unrelated to how routines vary.
n.2: A minor operational effect compared with the safety risk.
n.3: An inventory issue, not the principal risk.
n.4: Inconsistency is a process problem, not an equipment one.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to cover reception as well as assist chairside during a full list. What is the most appropriate response?
o: Accept and manage both roles as best they can
Explain the risk to patient care and agree priorities with the manager
Leave the surgery whenever the telephone rings
Refuse outright and continue chairside only
Take reception calls while assisting at the chairside
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Where workload threatens safe care, the concern should be raised and priorities agreed rather than absorbed.

n.0: Silently absorbing an unsafe workload leaves the risk in place.
n.2: Leaving a patient mid-treatment is unsafe.
n.3: A flat refusal without explanation does not resolve the staffing problem.
n.4: Breaks cross-infection control and divides attention from the patient.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A practice holds a meeting after a near miss involving the wrong instrument tray. What is the main purpose of discussing it as a team?
o: To agree who was at fault
To identify what allowed it to happen and change the system
To reassure staff that it was not serious
To record that the meeting took place
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Incident review should focus on the system that allowed the error, so the change prevents recurrence.

n.0: Fault-finding discourages reporting and rarely prevents recurrence.
n.1: Most incidents arise from systems rather than individuals.
n.3: A near miss is a warning that should be taken seriously.
n.4: A record is a by-product, not the purpose.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is preparing the surgery while the dentist is running late. Which action best supports the team?
o: Begin the appointment without the dentist
Prepare fully and let the next patient know the position
Send the patient away and rebook
Sit and wait until the dentist arrives
Start clearing down the previous surgery instead
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Supporting the team means having everything ready and keeping the patient informed about the delay.

n.0: Treatment cannot begin without the clinician.
n.2: Premature; the delay may be brief.
n.3: Wastes time that could be used to prepare.
n.4: Reasonable if already done, but the next patient still needs preparing and informing.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse feels a colleague is repeatedly leaving them to clear up alone. What is the best first step?
o: Complain to other members of staff
Do the same to them so the workload evens out
Raise it directly and calmly with the colleague
Raise it formally in writing to the practice owner
Say nothing and continue as before
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Most workload frictions are resolved by raising them directly and early, before escalation is needed.

n.0: Damages team relationships without resolving anything.
n.1: Retaliation makes the working environment worse.
n.3: Formal escalation before an informal conversation is disproportionate.
n.4: Resentment builds and the behaviour continues.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked by a colleague to sign a decontamination log for a cycle they did not witness. What should they do?
o: Decline, explaining that the record must reflect what they did
Sign it and note their concern separately
Sign it if the colleague confirms the cycle passed
Sign it provided the printout is attached
Sign it to avoid a delay to the list
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Records must reflect what the signatory actually did or witnessed; signing otherwise is a falsified record.

n.1: The false entry still stands in the record.
n.2: Confirmation is not the same as having witnessed it.
n.3: The signature attests to what that person did, not to the paperwork.
n.4: Convenience is never a reason to falsify a record.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A patient telephones asking to book directly with the hygienist for a scale and polish. What does direct access allow?
o: Hygienists may only see patients referred by a dentist
Hygienists may see patients directly for any treatment including whitening
Hygienists may see patients directly for their full scope except tooth whitening
Hygienists may see patients directly only for an examination
Hygienists may see patients directly only if a dentist is on the premises
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Under direct access, hygienists and therapists may carry out their full scope without prescription, with tooth whitening the exception.

n.0: This was the position before direct access was introduced.
n.1: Tooth whitening remains on prescription from a dentist.
n.3: Their scope is far wider than examination alone.
n.4: Direct access does not depend on a dentist being present.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A clinical dental technician wishes to see a patient without a dentist's prescription. For which work is this permitted?
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Clinical dental technicians may see patients directly for the provision and maintenance of complete dentures; other work needs a prescription.

n.0: Direct access for CDTs is limited to complete dentures.
n.2: Fixed prosthodontics is outside the CDT's direct scope.
n.3: Orthodontic work is not part of the CDT role.
n.4: Partial dentures require a dentist's prescription because the natural teeth must be assessed.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: An orthodontic therapist wishes to assess a patient without them seeing a dentist first. What may they carry out directly?
o: Index of Orthodontic Treatment Need screening
Plan the full course of orthodontic treatment
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Orthodontic therapists may carry out IOTN screening directly; the rest of their work is on prescription.

n.0: Carried out to the prescription of a dentist.
n.1: Requires a dentist's prescription where within scope at all.
n.3: Treatment planning is the dentist's responsibility.
n.4: Within scope but on prescription rather than direct.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked what 'scope of practice' means. Which definition is most accurate?
o: The list of duties written in the employment contract
The range of treatments the practice offers
What the practice owner permits a registrant to do
What you are trained, competent and registered to do
Whatever a registrant feels able to attempt
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Scope of practice is the area in which a registrant has the training, competence and registration to work safely.

n.0: A contract cannot extend what the GDC permits.
n.1: Describes the practice, not the individual registrant.
n.2: An employer cannot widen a registrant's scope.
n.4: Confidence is not competence.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental technician asks to observe a patient's appointment to understand a case better. What is the position?
o: Technicians may attend only if they hold a CDT qualification
Technicians may attend with the patient's consent and the clinician's agreement
Technicians may attend without consent as they are registrants
Technicians may never enter a clinical area
Technicians must first complete a chairside course
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Anyone additional in the surgery requires the patient's consent; registration alone does not confer a right to be present.

n.0: CDT registration governs treating patients, not observing.
n.2: Registration does not override the patient's consent.
n.3: There is no such blanket prohibition.
n.4: Observation is not the same as assisting.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: During a medical emergency, several team members respond at once. What best supports an effective response?
o: Everyone attempting the same task to be certain it is done
Everyone waiting for the most senior person to arrive
One person taking the lead and allocating clear roles
The first person on scene managing everything alone
Working without discussion to save time
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Emergencies are managed best when one person leads and roles are allocated explicitly.

n.0: Duplication leaves other essential tasks undone.
n.1: Delay in an emergency costs outcomes.
n.3: One person cannot do compressions, call for help and fetch the AED.
n.4: Silent working leads to gaps and duplication.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is unsure whether a task falls within their role. What is the safest course of action?
o: Ask the patient whether they mind
Attempt it carefully and review afterwards
Check the GDC scope of practice guidance and ask the clinician
Do it if a colleague has done it before
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Uncertainty about scope is resolved by checking the GDC guidance and discussing it with the clinician.

n.0: A patient cannot authorise work outside a registrant's scope.
n.1: Care does not make an out-of-scope task acceptable.
n.3: A colleague's practice may itself be wrong.
n.4: Refusal may be right, but the position should be checked and explained.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to sign for a delivery of prescription-only medicines. What is the main consideration?
o: Any staff member may sign for any delivery
Only a GDC registrant may accept the delivery
Only the practice owner may sign for deliveries
The delivery must be checked against the order and stored securely by an authorised person
The delivery should be left in reception until the dentist returns
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Medicines must be checked against the order and moved promptly to secure storage by someone authorised to do so.

n.0: Medicines require checking and secure storage, not just a signature.
n.1: Registration alone is not the relevant control.
n.2: Practices commonly authorise others; the control is the process.
n.4: Leaves medicines unsecured in a public area.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse notices stock of a critical item is running low during a busy week. What is the most appropriate action?
o: Borrow from another surgery without recording it
Order more and inform whoever manages stock
Substitute a similar product without telling anyone
Use the remaining stock sparingly and say nothing
Wait until it runs out before raising it
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Shortages should be flagged and reordered before the item runs out, through whoever holds responsibility for stock.

n.0: Moves the shortage rather than resolving it.
n.2: An unrecorded substitution may not be clinically equivalent.
n.3: Rationing a clinical item risks compromising care.
n.4: Leaves the practice without an item it needs.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A student on placement asks a dental nurse whether they can carry out a task alone. What should guide the answer?
o: The student's confidence in their own ability
What the student did at their previous placement
What the student has been assessed as competent to do, under supervision
Whether the practice is busy that day
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Students work within what they have been assessed as competent to do, and under appropriate supervision.

n.0: Students often over- or under-estimate their readiness.
n.1: Assessment is specific to the setting and the supervisor.
n.3: Workload never determines what a student may do.
n.4: Apparent simplicity is not an assessment of competence.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is handed a laboratory case with an incomplete prescription. What is the most appropriate action?
o: Complete the missing details from the patient's notes
Return it to the clinician to complete before it is sent
Send it and telephone the details through later
Send it as it is and let the laboratory query it
Write the details in yourself and initial them
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The laboratory prescription is the clinician's instruction and must be complete before the case leaves the practice.

n.0: The prescription is the clinician's instruction, not a transcription exercise.
n.2: Verbal additions are easily mis-recorded.
n.3: Causes delay and risks the technician guessing.
n.4: Amounts to writing a prescription the nurse cannot give.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to witness a colleague's signature on a consent form. What does witnessing confirm?
o: That the consent discussion was adequate
That the patient understood the treatment
That the patient was given written information
That the signature was made by the person named
That the treatment plan is clinically appropriate
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Witnessing a signature confirms only who signed it, not that valid consent was obtained.

n.0: The witness may not have heard the discussion at all.
n.1: Understanding is established in the discussion, not by a witness.
n.2: A witness does not attest to what was provided.
n.4: Clinical judgement is not part of witnessing.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A patient makes a complaint about their treatment at reception. What does the GDC require a practice to have?
o: A clear and effective complaints procedure
A policy of referring all complaints to the GDC
A written apology prepared in advance
An indemnity claim form for the patient
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: One of the nine GDC principles requires practices to have a clear and effective complaints procedure.

n.1: Legal involvement is rarely needed and is not a requirement.
n.2: Most complaints are resolved locally.
n.3: An apology should be specific to what happened.
n.4: Complaints are not claims and should not be treated as such.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A patient complains about a colleague's manner. What is the most appropriate immediate response?
o: Agree with the patient to calm the situation
Defend the colleague and explain they are very experienced
Explain that complaints must be made in writing
Listen, apologise that they feel this way and follow the complaints procedure
Tell the patient to raise it with the colleague directly
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Complaints are received by listening, acknowledging how the patient feels and following the practice procedure.

n.0: Agreeing before the facts are known is unfair to the colleague.
n.1: Dismisses the concern before it has been heard.
n.2: A barrier that discourages legitimate concerns.
n.4: Puts the patient in an uncomfortable position.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse becomes aware that a child attending the practice may be at risk of harm. What should they do?
o: Discuss it with the child's parent first
Follow the practice safeguarding procedure and raise it with the safeguarding lead
Keep a private note in case it happens again
Record it in the clinical notes and take no further action
Wait for clearer evidence before acting
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Safeguarding concerns are escalated through the practice procedure to the safeguarding lead, without waiting for proof.

n.0: May place the child at greater risk if the parent is involved.
n.2: A private note protects nobody.
n.3: Recording is necessary but not sufficient.
n.4: Safeguarding concerns are raised on concern, not on proof.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse posts a photograph from the surgery on social media with no patient visible. What is the main risk?
o: Identifiable details may still appear in the background
It breaches copyright held by the practice
Photographs may only be taken on practice equipment
The image quality may reflect badly on the practice
There is no risk if no patient is shown
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Backgrounds frequently contain identifiable information such as screens, records or appointment lists.

n.1: Copyright is not the principal professional concern.
n.2: Equipment used is not the issue.
n.3: Presentation is trivial beside confidentiality.
n.4: Notes, screens, appointment books and name badges can all identify people.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to give a reference for a colleague they have concerns about. What is the professional approach?
o: Decline to comment on anything negative
Give an honest and fair account of what they know
Give only positive comments to avoid difficulty
Refuse to provide any reference at all
Repeat what other colleagues have said
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: References should be honest and fair, based on what the referee knows first hand.

n.0: A partial account can mislead the recipient.
n.2: Risks a patient safety issue moving elsewhere.
n.3: Sometimes appropriate, but avoidance is not the professional default.
n.4: Hearsay is not a fair basis for a reference.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A patient asks a dental nurse for their personal phone number to ask questions later. What is the most appropriate response?
o: Explain that contact should go through the practice
Give a personal email address instead
Give it only for use during working hours
Give it, as it may help the patient
Take the patient's number and contact them instead
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Professional contact runs through the practice so that it is recorded, covered and appropriately boundaried.

n.1: The same boundary and record-keeping problems apply.
n.2: The boundary problem is unchanged by the hours.
n.3: Blurs the professional boundary and leaves advice unrecorded.
n.4: Still creates a private channel outside the record.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse realises they recorded a treatment entry against the wrong patient. What is the correct action?
o: Amend it correctly, showing the change and the reason
Delete the entry so the record is clean
Leave it and add a note to the correct patient's record
Report it only if the patient notices
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Errors in records are corrected transparently, leaving the original visible along with the reason for the change.

n.1: Deleting destroys the audit trail.
n.2: Leaves an incorrect entry on someone else's record.
n.3: An undocumented change looks like concealment.
n.4: Correction is required regardless of who notices.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is offered a gift by a grateful patient. What is the main professional consideration?
o: Gifts are always prohibited in dentistry
Gifts must be declared to the GDC
Gifts must be shared equally among the team
Whether accepting could affect, or appear to affect, patient care
Whether the gift is worth more than the treatment
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The question is whether accepting could influence care or be perceived to, which is why practices hold a gifts policy.

n.0: Small tokens of thanks are not banned outright.
n.1: Declaration is to the practice under its own policy, not routinely to the GDC.
n.2: A practical courtesy, not the professional test.
n.4: Value matters, but the test is influence and perception.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse wants to check that the practice's clinical protocols remain current. Which activity best supports this?
o: Asking long-serving staff what they usually do
Comparing them with the practice next door
Participating in audit and reviewing current guidance
Relying on what was taught during training
Waiting for an inspection to identify any gaps
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Audit against current published guidance is how a practice confirms its protocols remain appropriate.

n.0: Custom is not evidence that practice is current.
n.1: Another practice may be equally out of date.
n.3: Guidance changes, sometimes substantially.
n.4: Inspection is a check, not a method of keeping current.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse has been asked to complete an audit of hand hygiene compliance. What is the purpose of the audit cycle?
o: To compare staff against one another
To demonstrate activity to the practice insurer
To measure practice, make changes and then re-measure
To produce a report for the annual meeting
To satisfy a requirement to hold documents
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: An audit cycle measures current practice, implements change and then measures again to show whether it improved.

n.0: Audit examines the system, not individual performance rankings.
n.1: Not the purpose, even if it may be referenced.
n.3: A report is an output, not the aim.
n.4: Audit without re-measurement changes nothing.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse plans to take on radiography duties. What must be in place before they begin?
o: A note in the practice diary
Appropriate training and entitlement under IRMER
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Taking radiographs requires appropriate training and entitlement as an operator under IRMER.

n.0: Administration does not confer entitlement.
n.2: Patients consent to the exposure, not to who is entitled to take it.
n.3: A colleague cannot entitle someone under the regulations.
n.4: Experience is not the qualification required.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse completes an in-house training session delivered by the practice. Can this count as verifiable CPD?
o: Yes, automatically, as it takes place at work
Yes, but only if an external speaker delivers it
Yes, but only up to five hours per cycle
Yes, if it has aims, objectives, outcomes and documented evidence
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Verifiable CPD requires stated aims and objectives, anticipated outcomes and documentary evidence, wherever it is delivered.

n.0: In-house activity counts where the criteria are met.
n.1: Location does not make an activity verifiable.
n.2: The speaker's origin is not the test.
n.3: No such cap exists.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse has recorded 50 hours but all in the final year of the cycle. What is the problem?
o: Hours must be evenly spread across all five years
The minimum of ten hours in every two-year period was not met
The total should have been 100 hours
There is no problem provided the total is reached
They should have declared the hours monthly
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Reaching the total is not sufficient; at least ten hours must fall within every consecutive two-year period.

n.0: Even spread is not required, only the two-year minimum.
n.2: That is the requirement for dentists, not dental nurses.
n.3: The two-year minimum is a separate requirement.
n.4: Declaration is annual.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse wants their CPD to address a weakness identified at appraisal. Which activity is most appropriate?
o: A course chosen because colleagues are attending
A course directly addressing the identified weakness
A repeat of a course completed two years ago
The course with the highest number of hours
The next course the practice happens to book
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: CPD should be selected to address needs identified through appraisal and reflection.

n.0: Convenient, but not driven by need.
n.2: Repetition without a new need adds little.
n.3: Hours are not a measure of relevance.
n.4: Availability is not the same as suitability.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked what happens if the GDC audits their CPD. What should they be able to produce?
o: A letter from their employer confirming attendance
Evidence of the activities declared, mapped to development outcomes
Only the total number of hours claimed
Their original dental nursing qualification certificate
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: A CPD audit asks for the evidence behind declared activity, including how each maps to a development outcome.

n.0: An employer letter is not provider evidence.
n.1: Recollection is not evidence.
n.3: The audit examines the underlying activities.
n.4: Relates to registration, not to CPD.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to train a colleague in a task they carry out daily. What should they confirm first?
o: That the colleague is confident to try it
That the patient has agreed to the training
That the practice is quiet enough that day
That the task falls within the colleague's scope of practice
That they have trained someone before
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Training can only be given for tasks that fall within the recipient's scope of practice.

n.0: Confidence does not establish that the task is permitted.
n.1: Consent matters where a patient is involved, but scope comes first.
n.2: A practical matter rather than the professional test.
n.4: Experience of training is useful but not the first check.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is told by a colleague to 'just sign the sterilisation log, everyone does'. What does this most likely indicate?
o: A cultural problem that should be raised as a concern
A minor administrative shortcut of no consequence
A practice policy that should simply be followed
An acceptable practice during busy periods
An issue for the practice manager's annual review
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Normalised falsification of safety records is a cultural warning sign and should be raised as a concern.

n.1: The log evidences that instruments are safe to use.
n.2: No policy can require a false record.
n.3: Pressure does not make falsification acceptable.
n.4: Too slow for a patient safety issue.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: Two members of the dental team give a patient conflicting post-operative advice. What is the main risk?
o: The patient loses confidence and may follow the wrong advice
The practice may receive a poor online review
The record will be difficult to complete
The team will need an extra meeting
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Conflicting advice undermines confidence and may lead the patient to follow the less safe instruction.

n.0: A scheduling consequence rather than the clinical risk.
n.2: Reputation is secondary to patient safety.
n.3: An administrative side effect.
n.4: A response to the problem, not the risk itself.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to work through their break to keep the list on time. What is the most appropriate response?
o: Agree, as patient care must always come first
Discuss the pressure on the list and agree a workable plan
Work through and raise it at the next appraisal
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Recurrent pressure on breaks is a scheduling problem to be discussed and solved, not absorbed.

n.0: Does not address the pressure causing the problem.
n.1: Fatigue itself becomes a risk to patient care.
n.3: Leaves the underlying scheduling problem unresolved.
n.4: Too late to affect the situation causing harm now.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A new agency nurse arrives for a single day's cover. What is most important before they begin clinical work?
o: A briefing on local procedures, emergency equipment and where things are
A copy of the practice's business plan
Confirmation of their preferred break times
Introduction to every patient on the list
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Temporary staff need a local induction covering procedures and emergency arrangements before working clinically.

n.1: Irrelevant to safe clinical working.
n.2: A courtesy, not a safety requirement.
n.3: Impractical and unnecessary.
n.4: Administrative and unrelated to patient safety.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to update the practice's emergency drug stock list. Which check is most important?
o: That every item is the cheapest available
That expiry dates are checked and near-expiry items replaced
That the list matches last year's exactly
That the packaging is undamaged only
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Emergency drugs must be in date and replaced before expiry, since they are only used when time is critical.

n.0: Cost is irrelevant to emergency preparedness.
n.2: Tidy, but it does not make the drugs usable.
n.3: Guidance and stock requirements change.
n.4: Necessary but insufficient; an in-date check is the priority.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is unsure who to raise a clinical concern with. What should the practice have in place?
o: A named person and a clear route for raising concerns
A requirement to raise concerns only in writing
A rule that concerns go straight to the GDC
An annual meeting at which concerns are collected
An expectation that concerns are raised with the patient
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Practices should have a named person and a clear, accessible route so concerns can be raised promptly.

n.1: A written-only rule deters people from speaking up.
n.2: Most concerns are resolved locally first.
n.3: Far too slow for a patient safety issue.
n.4: Patients are not the route for staff concerns.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is told their concern has been noted but nothing changes. What is the appropriate next step?
o: Accept the decision and take no further action
Discuss it with patients so they are aware
Escalate through the practice's agreed procedure
Resign if it is not resolved
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: If a concern is not acted on, it should be escalated through the agreed route, and beyond the practice if necessary.

n.0: If patients remain at risk the duty to act continues.
n.1: Breaches confidentiality and is not the escalation route.
n.3: Unprofessional and likely to breach confidentiality.
n.4: Leaving does not protect the patients who remain.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse notices the practice's decontamination policy has not been reviewed for four years. Why does this matter?
o: Policies must be rewritten every twelve months by law
Practice may no longer reflect current guidance
Staff will have memorised it by now
The document will be difficult to read
The policy will have been lost from the system
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Guidance changes; an unreviewed policy may direct staff to practice that is no longer current.

n.0: There is no fixed statutory rewriting interval.
n.2: Familiarity with an out-of-date policy is a risk, not a benefit.
n.3: Age does not affect legibility.
n.4: Availability is a separate issue.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to help write a practice protocol. What should it be based on?
o: Current national guidance and the practice's own risk assessment
Custom and practice within the team
The preferences of the most senior clinician
The protocol used at a previous employer
Whatever is quickest to carry out
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Protocols are built from current national guidance, adapted through the practice's own risk assessment.

n.1: Habit is not evidence.
n.2: Seniority is not a source of guidance.
n.3: May be out of date or unsuited to this practice.
n.4: Speed is not a clinical standard.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is completing an incident report. Which detail is most important to include?
o: A factual account of what happened and when
An opinion on who was responsible
Reassurance that it will not recur
Which staff were on duty that week
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Incident reports should record the facts: what happened, when, and what was done in response.

n.1: Attribution of blame belongs to investigation, not the report.
n.2: May be relevant but is not the core content.
n.3: A promise cannot be made before the cause is understood.
n.4: Too broad to be useful.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to induct a new colleague into decontamination duties. What should the induction cover first?
o: The location of the staff room and lockers
The practice's decontamination policy and the equipment in use
The rota for the coming month
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Induction into a safety-critical role starts with the policy and the equipment the person will actually use.

n.0: Useful orientation but not safety critical.
n.2: Administrative rather than clinical.
n.3: Procurement detail.
n.4: An employment matter.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse observes that a colleague never checks the patient's identity before treatment. What is the risk?
o: The patient may be charged the wrong fee
The practice may lose the patient's contact details
Treatment may be carried out on the wrong patient
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Positive identification before treatment is what prevents the wrong patient receiving the wrong care.

n.0: A scheduling consequence, not the safety risk.
n.1: A real risk, but secondary to treating the wrong person.
n.2: A financial error rather than a clinical one.
n.3: Unrelated to identity checking at the chair.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to record that a colleague completed a task that they did not witness. Which principle applies?
o: Records may be completed by whoever is available
Records may be estimated if the detail is minor
Records must be accurate and reflect what actually happened
Records only need to be accurate for clinical procedures
Records should reflect what was intended to happen
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Records must be an accurate account of what happened, made by someone in a position to know.

n.0: Availability does not make an entry accurate.
n.1: Estimation in a safety record is falsification.
n.3: Decontamination and safety records matter equally.
n.4: Intent and outcome are not the same thing.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse wants to know whether a new team member is competent for a task. What is the most reliable evidence?
o: A verbal assurance from the person themselves
Direct observation against an agreed standard
How long they have worked in dentistry
Whether they hold any dental qualification
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Competence is established by observing the person perform the task against an agreed standard.

n.0: Self-assessment is unreliable in both directions.
n.2: Years worked is not the same as competence in this task.
n.3: Tells you nothing about this individual.
n.4: A qualification is broad; competence is task-specific.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to take on a lead role for infection control. What should accompany this responsibility?
o: A pay rise before the role begins
Appropriate training, time and authority to act
Sole responsibility for all decontamination tasks
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: A lead role needs training, protected time and enough authority to make the changes it identifies.

n.0: Reasonable to discuss, but not what makes the role workable.
n.2: Lead roles are usually held alongside clinical work.
n.3: A lead coordinates; they do not do everything.
n.4: Disciplinary matters sit with management.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A practice introduces a new decontamination procedure. What best supports consistent adoption?
o: A notice displayed in the decontamination room
Circulating the procedure by email to all staff
Discussing it at the next practice meeting
Training for everyone affected, with the written procedure available
Updating the policy folder and telling the senior nurse
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: New procedures are adopted consistently when everyone affected is trained and can access the written version.

n.0: Easily overlooked and offers no chance to ask questions.
n.1: Circulation is not the same as understanding.
n.2: Useful, but a discussion is not training.
n.4: Relies on information passing down accurately.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to comment on a colleague's performance during an investigation. What is the professional approach?
o: Decline to say anything at all
Describe only what they personally observed
Give a general impression of the colleague
Repeat what others in the team have said
Say only positive things to protect the colleague
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Contributions to an investigation should be limited to what the person directly observed.

n.0: Withholding relevant first-hand information may leave patients at risk.
n.2: Impressions are not evidence.
n.3: Hearsay is unreliable and unfair.
n.4: Loyalty does not outweigh patient safety.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A practice has not brought the team together for several months. Why should a dental practice hold regular team meetings?
o: So the practice can demonstrate activity to inspectors
To allow decisions to be made without the clinical team
To record attendance for employment purposes
To reduce the amount of written communication
To share information, review incidents and agree changes
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Team meetings exist so information is shared, incidents reviewed and changes agreed collectively.

n.0: Evidence is a by-product, not the purpose.
n.1: The point is to include the team, not exclude it.
n.2: An administrative side effect.
n.3: Meetings supplement written communication rather than replacing it.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse disagrees with an instruction they believe is unsafe. What should they do?
o: Carry it out and record their disagreement afterwards
Carry it out since the clinician is responsible
Raise the concern before acting and escalate if unresolved
Seek a second opinion from the patient
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Concerns about safety are raised before acting; a registrant remains accountable for what they do.

n.0: The harm may already have occurred.
n.1: Each registrant is accountable for their own actions.
n.3: Refusal may be right, but the concern must be explained and escalated.
n.4: Patients cannot adjudicate clinical safety.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse's registration lapses because they forgot to renew. What is the consequence?
o: There is no consequence if the fee is paid late
They may continue working while the renewal is processed
They may work only under supervision until it is restored
They must inform the patient at each appointment
They must stop practising until registration is restored
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: It is unlawful to practise dentistry while unregistered; work must stop until registration is restored.

n.0: Registration lapses regardless of intention.
n.1: Working unregistered is a criminal offence.
n.2: Supervision does not substitute for registration.
n.3: Disclosure does not make unregistered practice lawful.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to describe what makes feedback to a colleague effective. Which approach is best?
o: Deliver it in front of the team so everyone learns
Give it only at the annual appraisal
Give it privately, promptly and based on specific observations
Raise it through a third party to avoid awkwardness
Wait until several issues have accumulated
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Feedback works when it is private, timely and anchored to specific things that were observed.

n.0: Public criticism humiliates rather than teaches.
n.1: Feedback months later cannot change the behaviour.
n.3: Indirect feedback distorts and damages trust.
n.4: An accumulated list feels like an ambush.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is told the practice will start offering a new treatment. What should they establish about their own role?
o: How much the treatment will cost patients
What training they need and whether it falls within their scope
Whether it will change their working hours
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Before assisting with anything new, a registrant establishes whether it is within scope and what training is required.

n.0: Commercial detail rather than a professional question.
n.2: An employment matter.
n.3: Irrelevant to their own competence.
n.4: Does not affect what they may safely do.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse repeatedly finds equipment left uncleaned by the previous session. What is the most constructive response?
o: Clean it each time and say nothing
Leave it and report each occurrence to the GDC
Raise it with the team and agree a clear end-of-session standard
Refuse to use the surgery until it is resolved
Speak to patients about the standards
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Recurring process failures are solved by agreeing a shared standard rather than by individuals absorbing them.

n.0: The problem repeats and the risk continues.
n.1: Disproportionate before any local attempt to resolve it.
n.3: Disrupts patient care rather than fixing the process.
n.4: Unprofessional and unhelpful.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A new nurse asks why procedures are written down when everyone already knows them. What is the main purpose of a practice keeping written protocols rather than relying on custom?
o: To ensure consistent, current practice that can be checked
To give the practice something to show inspectors
To prevent staff having to think for themselves
To reduce the amount of training needed
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Written protocols make practice consistent, reviewable against current guidance and auditable.

n.1: Inspection is a check, not the purpose.
n.2: Protocols support judgement rather than replacing it.
n.3: A protocol does not remove the need for training.
n.4: A useful side effect, not the reason.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse completes CPD on a topic unrelated to their role. Can it count?
o: No, all CPD must relate directly to dental nursing
Yes, but only if the practice paid for it
Yes, but only up to ten hours per cycle
Yes, if it is relevant to their practice and maps to a development outcome
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: CPD must be relevant to the registrant's practice and map to a development outcome, but need not be narrowly clinical.

n.0: Broader learning can be relevant, for example communication or leadership.
n.1: Who funds the activity is irrelevant.
n.2: No such cap exists.
n.4: Relevance and mapping are still required.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is preparing for their first appraisal. What would make it most useful to them?
o: Arriving with no preparation so it is spontaneous
Asking a colleague what they said in theirs
Bringing examples of their work and reflections on what went well and less well
Preparing a list of complaints about the practice
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Appraisal is most useful when the individual brings evidence and honest reflection to discuss.

n.0: An unprepared appraisal produces little of value.
n.1: Their development needs are not yours.
n.3: An employment document, not a development one.
n.4: Concerns may be raised, but appraisal is about development.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A nurse is assembling their CPD evidence and cannot find one certificate. What should a dental nurse do if they realise a CPD certificate has been lost?
o: Ask the provider for a replacement record
Claim the hours as non-verifiable instead
Omit the activity entirely from the record
Write their own confirmation of attendance
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Providers can usually reissue evidence; the registrant should request a replacement rather than improvise.

n.1: The activity was verifiable; the evidence simply needs replacing.
n.2: Estimation is not evidence.
n.3: Loses hours that were legitimately earned.
n.4: Self-certification is not provider evidence.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked whether they may apply fluoride varnish. What determines the answer?
o: Whether the dentist is in the building
Whether the practice has stock available
Whether they have completed appropriate training for the skill
Whether they have worked in the practice for a year
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Applying fluoride varnish is an additional skill requiring appropriate training before it may be undertaken.

n.0: Presence does not extend another registrant's scope.
n.1: A request cannot authorise an untrained task.
n.2: Availability is unrelated to competence.
n.4: Length of service is not training.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is unclear whether an activity counts towards their CPD total. Where should they check?
o: The opinion of the course provider alone
What colleagues have counted in the past
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: The GDC publishes the criteria for verifiable CPD, and that is the authority to check against.

n.1: Providers have an interest in their courses counting.
n.2: CPD is a matter between the registrant and the GDC.
n.3: Colleagues may have been wrong.
n.4: Appearance is not a criterion.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to describe reflective practice. Which description is most accurate?
o: Recording the hours spent on each activity
Repeating a task until it becomes automatic
Reviewing an experience to identify what to do differently
Writing down everything that happened during a session
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Reflection examines an experience to draw out what would be done differently in future.

n.0: That is CPD record keeping.
n.1: That is practice, not reflection.
n.3: A summary describes content rather than learning.
n.4: A description is not a reflection.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked to check that a colleague's radiography entitlement is current. Why does this matter?
o: Entitlement determines who may lawfully carry out an exposure
It affects how the exposure is charged
It determines the equipment settings used
It governs how images are stored
It is needed for the practice's CPD returns
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Only entitled and trained operators may carry out exposures under IRMER; entitlement must be current.

n.1: Charging is unrelated to entitlement.
n.2: Settings depend on the examination, not the operator's paperwork.
n.3: Storage is a separate requirement.
n.4: CPD and IRMER entitlement are different things.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse wants to raise a concern but fears it will affect their job. What protection exists?
o: Concerns may only be raised anonymously
Concerns must be raised through a solicitor
Protection applies only to clinicians, not nurses
Raising concerns in the public interest is protected in law
There is no protection for staff who raise concerns
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Workers raising concerns in the public interest have legal protection, and the GDC expects concerns to be raised.

n.0: Anonymity is an option, not a requirement or the source of protection.
n.1: Legal representation is not needed to raise a concern.
n.2: Protection is not restricted by role.
n.4: Whistleblowing protections exist in law.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse notices the practice has no record of who checked the autoclave this week. What is the risk?
o: Instruments may have been released without verified cycles
The autoclave may use more electricity
The practice may be charged for a service visit
The staff rota may be inaccurate
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Without cycle records there is no evidence that instruments used on patients were properly sterilised.

n.1: Trivial beside the safety issue.
n.2: A commercial consequence.
n.3: Financial rather than clinical.
n.4: Unrelated.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked what 'accountability' means for a registrant. Which description is most accurate?
o: Being answerable for your own decisions and actions
Being responsible for the whole team's conduct
Holding a management position in the practice
Reporting to the GDC every year
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Every registrant is personally answerable for their own decisions and actions, whoever asked them to act.

n.1: Accountability is personal, not collective.
n.2: Instructions do not remove personal accountability.
n.3: Accountability applies to every registrant.
n.4: That is the annual declaration, not accountability itself.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is offered a place on a course during working hours. What should they establish with the practice?
o: How the course will be paid for only
That the time is agreed and cover arranged
Whether it is the cheapest option available
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Attending during working hours requires agreement on the time and arrangements for clinical cover.

n.0: Important, but not the operational question.
n.2: Irrelevant to attending it themselves.
n.3: Cost is secondary to relevance and arrangements.
n.4: A practical detail rather than a professional one.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse is asked how they know the practice's infection control is effective. What provides the best evidence?
o: Audit results and cycle records reviewed over time
Staff say they follow the policy
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Effectiveness is evidenced by audit and by the records showing cycles met their parameters over time.

n.1: Absence of complaints is not evidence of safety.
n.2: Self-report is not measurement.
n.3: New equipment can still be used incorrectly.
n.4: Appearance is not decontamination.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A nurse assumes their employer will arrange their required learning for the year. Who is responsible for a registrant's continuing professional development?
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: CPD is a personal obligation of registration; the registrant plans, completes, records and declares it.

n.0: The GDC sets requirements; it does not allocate learning.
n.2: May support and fund CPD but does not hold the obligation.
n.3: An employer may help, but the duty is personal.
n.4: Involvement ends with the qualification.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse wishes to move into a practice manager role. What is the most appropriate first step?
o: Apply for roles and learn once appointed
Discuss it at appraisal and plan the development needed
Take on the duties informally without discussion
Wait to be offered the role
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Career development is planned through appraisal, identifying what learning is needed before the move.

n.0: Leaves gaps that may affect performance and patients.
n.2: Disproportionate as a first step.
n.3: Creates ambiguity about responsibility.
n.4: Career development rarely happens passively.

Professional Development & Teamwork.q: A dental nurse notices that the practice never reviews incidents once they are recorded. What is the consequence?
o: Incidents will be recorded more quickly
Records will become difficult to store
The practice will run out of forms
The same failures are likely to recur
The team will become complacent about recording
Professional Development & Teamwork.w: Recording without review changes nothing; the value of an incident system is in acting on what it shows.

n.0: Speed of recording is unaffected.
n.1: A storage matter, not a safety one.
n.2: Trivial.
n.4: A likely side effect, but not the primary consequence.
